queries.text: Along the Riccati (vHJ / Hamilton-Jacobi) curvature flow for the Hessian of the time-dependent log density, why does a continuity argument keep the supremum of the weighted deviation from a fixed reference precision matrix below the smaller root of a quadratic majorant, and how does that curvature floor give a lower bound on the conditional Poincare (spectral gap) constant in terms of the smallest eigenvalue of the reference precision?

Hessian defect confinement under the matrix Riccati equation: the weighted distance between the time-dependent log-density Hessian and a reference Gaussian precision cannot cross the smaller root of a quadratic majorant, and the resulting curvature floor yields a conditional spectral gap bound through the reference's smallest eigenvalue (Brascamp-Lieb / Bakry-Emery).

Why is the supremum over time of the weighted deviation of the log-density Hessian from a fixed reference precision confined below the smaller of the two roots of a quadratic majorant (a Riccati comparison / curvature defect bound), and how does that confinement convert into a lower bound on the conditional gap in terms of the reference precision's smallest eigenvalue?

Dynamic Hessian Riccati flow: the curvature defect relative to a Gaussian reference precision stays below the smaller quadratic root; the conditional Poincare constant is bounded below by the smallest eigenvalue of the reference precision reduced by that defect.
